chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Jaroud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The most beloved of deeds to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is causing gladness to enter upon a believer: satisfying a Muslim's hunger or fulfilling his debt.'
ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved deeds to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates 'introducing joy' (idkhal al-surur) to a supreme act of worship, linking spiritual merit directly to tangible social welfare. By specifying feeding the hungry and settling debts, it underscores the practical dimensions of faith, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on alleviating the socio-economic burdens of the community as a means of drawing near to God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Al Jaroud, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard himasws saying: ‘The most beloved of the deeds to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is to cause the entering of the gladness upon the Momin, satiating a Muslim, or fulfilling his debts’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from abu al-Jarud from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘The most beloved of deeds to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is bringing joy to the heart of a believer, by means of satisfying his hunger or paying off his debt.’”
